overview: Holywell Bay is a big, sandy beach about three miles south-west of Newquay, backed by a huge system of dunes that’s around 5,000 years old and one of the largest in Britain. It faces north-west into the Atlantic, has lifeguards in summer and is popular for surfing.
On the north side of the beach is a sea cave with St Cubert’s holy well inside, the source of the bay’s name, though a cliff fall in 2026 has closed access to it.

expect.title: Dunes
expect.text: Vast dunes behind the beach; in summer people sandboard down them.

expect.title: Surf
expect.text: A popular surfing beach with lifeguard cover in season.

expect.title: Holy well cave
expect.text: The cave at the north end, with its mineral pools and holy well, is currently inaccessible after a cliff collapse in August 2026.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: In the parish of Cubert, about three miles west-south-west of Newquay.

goodToKnow.label: Holiday parks
goodToKnow.text: There are several holiday parks around Holywell, so it gets busy in peak season.

week.text: A great big-beach day near Newquay, with dunes for the children to tumble down. It faces north-west, so it’s lovely in the evening. Combine it with a walk over the headland to Porth Joke.

pairWith.why: a small unspoilt cove over the headland
miles of sand to the south

tips: Respect the cliff-fall warnings around the cave at the north end.
